source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 11 May 1939, p. 5 ("Local elections: No Contest for Down County Council"); Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1939, p. 12 ("Rural councils (nominations)"); Northern Whig, 4 May 1939, p. 10 ("Downpatrick: three contests are likely")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned without a contest: the nominations gave contests only in Downpatrick Rural, Ardglass and Castlewellan Urban (Northern Whig, 4 May 1939, p. 10); returned unopposed when S. Ryan (U.) and W. J. Guiness withdrew: 'Mr. Felix M'Kenna (Nat.), a former member of the Council, was returned unopposed as the representative for Castlewellan electoral division' (Belfast News-Letter, 11 May 1939, p. 5) (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the Downpatrick Rural District Council, polled at the end of May 1939. The two contested divisions, Ardglass and Downpatrick Rural, were counted on 2 June; Castlewellan Urban had three nominations, but two withdrew and Felix M'Kenna was returned unopposed (Belfast News-Letter, 11 May 1939, p. 5). Filed on 1939-06-01, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Down that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1939-05-31 (verification 5 Nov 2026). Killinchy and Raholp are recorded from the report of the new council's annual meeting of 7 June 1939, with their divisions from the 1930 return (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Three nominations (F. M'Kenna, W. J. Guiness, S. Ryan); Ryan and Guiness withdrew, so there was no poll (Belfast News-Letter, 4 and 11 May 1939). Returned unopposed.
